answer: Island-Tundra Bridge Sparsity: agents earn routing credit only by relaying across low-connectivity boundary edges (the tundra between dense island clusters). New nodes start with zero bridge credit; credit accrues per verified cross-cluster hop and decays without fresh bridging. A sybil swarm must physically split across many islands and sustain real relay traffic across sparse links, paying bandwidth, latency, and decay costs proportional to cluster count—costs that scale superlinearly with swarm size, while honest agents accrue credit at dawn of each epoch from genuine topology gaps.
